crossover_finding: C1 confirmed. dudect detects the nonce timing leaks (latency and address-data classes, 1/1 each) but MISSES the division-timing leak (KyberSlash) on this x86 divider. varlat DETECTS KyberSlash (the idiv on secret data, an instruction-level detection independent of measured time). timecop cannot see the variable-latency class at all, and is non-discriminating on the nonce pairs because it also flags OpenSSL's constant-time scalar multiplication. Three analysers, three different blind spots, measured on real deployed leaks. KyberSlash is tier C, so the varlat detection is a recorded outcome, not a recall-denominator entry; the crossover is nonetheless real.
note: Recall over applicable tier-A/B corpus pairs, per named class with its n. varlat has no tier-A/B recall entry because its detections are on tier-C KyberSlash; its harnesses for the tier-A ecdsa pairs are not built (recorded as inapplicable-no-harness, not a miss).
